title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.114
exact_target: Is there one universal upper bound on the derived lengths of all finite groups whose subgroups have no larger abelianization?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
For any finite group $H$, let $H'=[H,H]$ be its commutator subgroup, generated by $a^{-1}b^{-1}ab$ with $a,b\in H$. Its abelianization $H/H'$ is the largest abelian quotient of $H$, and its order is the index $[H:H']$.

A finite group $G$ is weakly ab-maximal if
\[
 [H:H']\le[G:G']\qquad\text{for every subgroup }H\le G.
\]
The inequality is weak, so subgroups may have abelianizations of the same order as that of $G$. The subgroups being tested need not be normal, and each is abelianized using its own commutator subgroup.

Define $G^{(0)}=G$ and $G^{(j+1)}=[G^{(j)},G^{(j)}]$. When $G^{(d)}=1$ for some $d$, its derived length is the least such nonnegative integer; otherwise assign derived length infinity.

Do weakly ab-maximal finite groups have bounded derived length? Precisely, is there an absolute integer $D\ge0$ such that
\[
 G^{(D)}=1\qquad\text{for every weakly ab-maximal finite group }G?
\]
The same $D$ must work simultaneously for all orders, all primes dividing those orders, and all numbers of generators. A bound depending on $|G|$ or on $[G:G']$ would not answer this uniform question. The hypothesis compares only the sizes of abelian quotients of subgroups, while the conclusion bounds the number of iterations of the derived operation.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Is there one universal upper bound on the derived lengths of all finite groups whose subgroups have no larger abelianization?
